subject.title: plugins.entries.<id>.subagent.allowModelOverride is ignored for interactive (client-scoped) subagent runs

question: Should the shipped `plugins.entries.<id>.subagent.allowModelOverride` grant authorize plugin subagent provider/model overrides from interactive and other request-scoped contexts, instead of only clientless background runs?
rationale: Current SDK docs and the reported workflow expect the opt-in to authorize subagent model overrides generally, but latest-release behavior and config help scope the key to background runs, so changing it widens a shipped authorization boundary.

options.title: Approve widened grant
options.body: Land or revise the linked PR so explicit plugin-scoped subagent trust applies in background and scoped contexts, bounded by `allowedModels` and non-transitive internal authority.

options.title: Narrow scoped contexts
options.body: Require a revised fix that covers interactive operator-scoped plugin runs while excluding external plugin HTTP route scopes if maintainers want that boundary preserved.

options.title: Keep background-only
options.body: Reject the behavior change and update SDK docs plus runtime errors so operators know this config key cannot authorize interactive plugin subagent overrides.

recommendation.title: Approve widened grant
recommendation.body: Land or revise the linked PR so explicit plugin-scoped subagent trust applies in background and scoped contexts, bounded by `allowedModels` and non-transitive internal authority.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman introduced the trusted plugin subagent override policy and related gateway docs, making them the strongest feature-history owner for the config-contract decision.
